title_now: Far-contra code on hits: partial return

pictures.crop_done: suptitle removed (render rows 128..600), as the current deck image; same 2040 x 472 px

notes_body: Frozen pre-stroke decoder (LP-trained), far-contra code retained = (far-contra score on the class - chance) / (pre-stroke hits - chance), per session with >= 5 trials; a hit cell needs >= 20 hits per animal x epoch (summed over its sessions); below it the session values are shown, not tested: acute PS92 (2 sessions, 10 hits) and PS94 (1 session, 8 hits; 7 in the pre-cue window) are gray hollow diamonds, outside the mean, SEM and CI; PS95 has no acute session with >= 5 hits (0); pre-cue (lick-free ENL), cue and lick windows. Chronic hits: lick -0.29 [-0.43, -0.13], cue -0.27 [-0.40, -0.14], pre-cue -0.27 [-0.45, -0.09] (CIs exclude 0). Failed attempts: change vs pre-stroke hits -0.79 to -0.98 acutely and -0.79 to -0.88 subacutely in every window (retained 0.02-0.21; every CI reaches 0 retained). Recovery timing on hits (exponential fits per animal): cortex half-recovery unresolved in all four (PS92 / PS94 / PS95 below 20 acute hits; PS93 never gets half-way back to pre); behavior half-recovery 6.7 / 5.7 / 8.3 days (PS92-94; PS95 at the fit bound). Neither predicts the other session to session (lagged model, 60 pairs: behavior[t] ~ cortex[t-1] +0.04 [-0.21, +0.35]; cortex[t] ~ behavior[t-1] +0.12 [-0.23, +0.43]). On behavior-matched trials cortex still responds differently and session-specific weights fit better -> a remapped, not restored, mapping (encoding page Figs 2.3 [#f-matched_residual], 4.1 [#f-selffit_cue]; not re-measured in this pass). Encoding page Figs 8.5 [#f-decoder_retention_pooled], 0.5 [#f-recovery_timing_lick]. Script scripts/decoder_retention_sessions.py.

title_now: Per animal: behavior full, code on hits not

pictures.crop_done: re-tiled 2 x 2 exactly as the current deck image (hit-rate panel over cortex panel per animal; PS94 quadrant takes column 1's y labels; seam at x 576), empty aim row + suptitle cut; the legend gained the '< 20 hits' entry and is split into two lines, so the image is 1043 x 1371 (was 1043 x 1338): fit by height (picture box ~2.4 % taller or ~2.4 % narrower)

notes_body: Per session, lick window: behavior = far-contra hit rate (contact / camera-working-period trials) / the animal's pre-stroke level; cortex = the FROZEN pre-stroke decoder's far-contra code on far-contra HITS only (sessions with >= 5 hits; an animal x epoch needs >= 20 hits), / pre level. Gray band = pre-stroke days. Half-recovery relative to pre from exponential fits per animal, 95 % CI by resampling sessions: behavior PS92 6.7 d [5.0, 8.7], PS93 5.7 d [4.3, 7.3], PS94 8.3 d [5.4, 12.1], PS95 at the fit bound (1.5 d); completeness 102 / 102 / 98 / 101 %. Cortex unresolved in all four: PS92 (10 acute hits), PS94 (8) and PS95 (0) are below 20 hits (the acute PS92 and PS94 sessions are drawn as gray hollow diamonds: shown, not in any fit or epoch value; PS95 has no acute session with >= 5 hits); PS93 (31 acute hits) recovers 38 % of its acute deficit and never gets half-way. Chronic code on hits / pre: PS92 0.76, PS93 0.60, PS94 0.55, PS95 0.94. Session to session neither predicts the other beyond its own past (behavior[t] ~ cortex[t-1] +0.04 [-0.21, +0.35]; cortex[t] ~ behavior[t-1] +0.12 [-0.23, +0.43]; 60 pairs, animal fixed effects). The render's aim row was empty (aim table not found under this run) and is cut, so the 'cortex - aim' entries in the cortex subtitles are unresolved by construction. Re-tiled from encoding page Fig 0.5 [#f-recovery_timing_lick]; script scripts/recovery_timing.py --window lick.

notes_body: Encoding page Fig 0.6 [#f-recovery_timing_pooled_epoch_lick]: the same as Fig 0.12 BY EPOCH, one marker per session, with the per-session GAP (cortex - behavior). Behavior = far-contra hit rate (contact / camera-working-period trials) / the animal's pre; cortex = FROZEN pre-stroke decoder's far-contra code on far-contra HITS (lick window), / pre. Change vs pre, nested bootstrap (animals -> sessions). Behavior: acute -0.94 [-0.99, -0.89], subacute -0.23 [-0.35, -0.13], chronic +0.01 [-0.03, +0.03] (fully back). Cortex on hits: acute not estimated (< 20 hits per animal x epoch in PS92 / PS94; their acute sessions, PS92 2 sessions / 10 hits and PS94 1 session / 8 hits, are drawn as gray hollow diamonds in the cortex and gap panels, outside the mean, SEM and CI; PS95 has no acute session with >= 5 hits), subacute -0.31 [-0.49, -0.15], chronic -0.29 [-0.43, -0.13]. Gap: subacute -0.09 [-0.26, +0.07], chronic -0.29 [-0.43, -0.14]: behavior recovers fully, the cortical far-contra code on successful trials does not; PS95 is the closest to full cortical recovery (chronic code 0.94 of pre). Licks: hit = camera contact class inside the camera working period (trial_attempts.csv); decoder lick window aligned to the first LP video lick. Script scripts/recovery_timing.py --window lick. Kept as one row of 3 panels: a 2-row tiling would make each panel smaller on this slide.

notes_body: Encoding page Fig 0.12 [#f-recovery_timing_pooled_day_lick] (image recovery_timing_pooled_day_lick_aim.png, all three panels). A (PRIMARY): far-contra AIM (first post-cue lick, 3-D angle minus the animal's pre mean at that spout, + = contralesional; all trials with a first lick, so acute aim is mostly failed attempts): -32 deg day 1, -15 days 6-7, -9 days 8-9, then about -5 to -6 deg from day 25 on, CI below 0 in every late bin; half-recovery relative to pre 8.8 / 6.8 / 13.5 / 4.5 days (PS92-95). Fraction of the acute aim deficit recovered by chronic: PS92 .84, PS93 .76, PS94 .55, PS95 .90 (hit rate 0.98-1.02 in all); the chronic residual is mostly PS94 (-13 to -21 deg in the chronic bins), the animal with the least code recovery too (chronic code 0.55 of pre; descriptive, n = 4). B: far-contra hit rate / pre: 0.03 day 1, 0.83 days 8-9, 0.94-1.03 from day 10 on. C: far-contra frozen code on hits / pre: 0.71 days 8-9, 0.61-0.80 from day 10 on (days 1-5 rest on 1-3 animals). Gray hollow diamonds in C = the acute code-on-hits sessions of PS92 (days 2 and 5, 10 hits) and PS94 (day 7, 8 hits), below the 20-hit minimum of the epoch tests; the day-bin means are not hit-gated, so they sit inside bins 2 (0.34), 5 (0.61) and 6-7 (0.68); PS95 has no acute session with >= 5 hits. The gap opens chronically, not acutely. Script scripts/recovery_timing.py --aim.
